title: Correct a Seatbelt Tongue Rotated on the Belt
introduction:
The tongue is the metal fitting that engages the seatbelt buckle. This adjustment uses a diagonal fold in the belt to change the tongue’s orientation as it slides over that fold—much like turning a ribbon through a narrow slot.

I use the drawings as a pair: the first establishes the fold beside the tongue, and the second shows the folded belt passing through the tongue’s slot. The intended result is a tongue that is no longer rotated on the belt. This adjustment addresses that orientation only; it is not a general seatbelt repair procedure.

edits.text: Fold the safety belt diagonally beside the tongue, matching the fold shown in the first drawing.
edits.why: The diagonal fold prepares the webbing to turn within the tongue’s slot as the tongue moves across it.

edits.text: Pull the safety belt tongue over the fold, allowing the folded section of belt to pass through the tongue’s slot as shown in the second drawing.
edits.why: Passing the tongue over the fold changes its orientation on the webbing. The drawing shows the folded belt within the slot during this movement.
